title: Sales/CS enterprise signal categorizer + scope canvas
creator: Aisha Park
description:
Problem: Sales and CS get a high volume of enterprise feature signals (requests, RFP asks, regulatory asks) that vary widely in urgency, complexity, and compliance needs. Currently there is manual, ad-hoc categorization leading to inconsistent first-pass scoping, duplication, and slow response windows for high-value accounts.

Objective: Create a lightweight, repeatable "Signal Categorizer" and a one-page "Scope Canvas" that Sales/CS can use to classify enterprise feature asks and produce a reliable initial effort estimate and routing recommendation within one business day. The toolset should be simple enough for reps to fill in during discovery and structured enough to allow PMs and Eng leads to do quick triage and prioritize backlog intake.

Outcomes we care about:
- Reduce time-to-first-scope for enterprise asks from ~5 business days to <=1 business day for 70% of incoming requests.
- Surface compliance or privacy flags early so Private/VPC/workload-sensitive requests are routed correctly.
- Provide a consistent effort-band estimate (S/M/L/XL) and risk band (low/medium/high) to accelerate prioritization.
- Exportable canvas that can be attached to Linear tickets and stored in a CRM record.

In-scope: design of categorization taxonomy, one-page scope canvas template, instructions and training for Sales/CS, minimal validation workflow in Linear for PM triage, sample routing rules.
Out-of-scope: full automation with CRM integration, engineering implementation of private deployment changes, SLA contract changes (these will be follow-ups if surfaced).

Success metrics (initial): time-to-first-scope median, percent of requests with compliance flag captured, % of asks triaged without follow-up questions, CS satisfaction score on intake process.
acceptance_criteria: Signal Categorizer doc describing required fields, definitions, and decision heuristics published to Confluence
One-page Scope Canvas template available as Google Doc and downloadable PDF
Sales/CS playbook with fill examples and routing matrix (hosted in Drive) shared with GTM reps
Sample Linear workflow created (ticket type, tags, and triage checklist) and validated in a staging workspace
Pilot with 3 major accounts run for two weeks and metrics collected: time-to-first-scope and compliance-flag capture rate
comments: 2025-03-12 Aisha Park: Created initial ticket after compaction workshop with Sales Ops and CS. Observed 27% of asks have missing compliance info which delays triage.

2025-03-14 Diego Martinez: Drafted taxonomy (signal_type, business_value_band, compliance_flag, latency_need, integration_complexity). Shared initial draft: https://docs.google.com/document/d/1SignalDraft
2025-03-16 Emily Chen (Sales): Suggested adding 'contractual change' checkbox because many asks are not product changes but contract terms. Added to canvas draft.

2025-03-17 Research note: Looked at 120 historical enterprise asks from last 12 months. ~35% would have been flagged as 'Private deployment' early based on customer attributes. Deck: https://company.atlassian.net/wiki/spaces/PM/pages/Enterprise+Intake+Analysis

2025-03-18 PM review: Added 'effort band' guidelines (S: 1-2 wks, M: 3-6 wks, L: 6-12 wks, XL: >12 wks) and mapping to expected engineering owners. Feedback: need a clear path for 'compliance_yes' -> security review flow.
2025-03-19 Design handoff: DES-2123 to create canvas visuals and embed examples. Link to Figma: https://www.figma.com/file/CanvasMockup

2025-03-20 Diego Martinez: Updated ticket with pilot plan and Linear workflow proposal. Created sample PR for triage checklist automation: https://github.com/redwood-inference/intake-worflow/pull/1284
decision_log: 2025-03-15 Decision: Use simple four-field primary classifier: signal_type (feature/contract/risk), business_value_band (low/med/high), compliance_flag (none/privacy/regulatory), and latency_need (normal/expedite). Rationale: balances speed and signal fidelity.
2025-03-18 Decision: Effort bands will be S/M/L/XL with suggested engineering owners; this is intentionally coarse to keep first-pass fast.
2025-03-19 Decision: Pilot will be limited to Sales AMER+EMEA with three named accounts before broader rollout. Rationale: faster feedback loop and high-impact signals.
